title: Lua
tagline: The small scripting language inside games and tools
description: Lua is small, fast and made to live inside other programs: games, game engines, editors, databases and network tools use it for their scripting. Starting from the first line, the course covers values and types, numbers, strings and input, decisions and loops, the table (Lua's one data structure, used as list, dictionary, record and object), functions, closures and recursion, the string library and Lua patterns, metatables, classes and inheritance, modules, errors, iterators, coroutines, files, how Lua is embedded in a C program, and finally sandboxes for untrusted code, weak tables and the garbage collector, and bitwise operators and binary data. Every lesson has checked practice that runs real Lua 5.4, and every milestone ends with a project.

milestones.title: First Steps
milestones.blurb: What Lua is and where it runs, values and types, local variables, numbers, strings and input, and decisions.

lessons.title: What Lua Is and Running Code
lessons.summary: Where Lua came from and where it runs today (games, editors, databases, network tools), how a Lua program runs from top to bottom, print, comments, and how to read an error message.

lessons.title: Values, Variables and Types
lessons.summary: Lua's eight types and the type function, nil as "no value", local variables and why every variable should be local, assigning several variables at once, and swapping two values.

lessons.title: Numbers and Arithmetic
lessons.summary: Integers and floats inside the one number type, the operators including / and // and ^, how % works with negatives, the math library, converting with tonumber and tostring, and rounding.

lessons.title: Strings and Input
lessons.summary: Writing strings with quotes, escapes and long brackets, joining with .., the length operator #, strings never changing, io.write versus print, and reading input with io.read and its formats.

lessons.title: Making Decisions
lessons.summary: if, elseif and else, the comparison operators with ~= for "not equal", what counts as true (everything except false and nil), and, or and not and what they return, and the x or default idiom.

milestones.title: Loops and Tables
milestones.blurb: while, repeat and for loops, tables as lists and as dictionaries, the table library, and nested tables and copies.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.summary: The numeric for loop with its start, stop and step, while and repeat-until, break, skipping to the next round with goto continue, and the loop variable belonging to the loop.

lessons.title: Tables as Lists
lessons.summary: The table as Lua's only data structure, lists that start at index 1, the length operator, adding and removing with table.insert and table.remove, ipairs, and why holes in a list break #.

lessons.title: Tables as Dictionaries
lessons.summary: Tables with any keys, the dot shorthand for string keys, records, adding and removing with nil, pairs and its order, counting and grouping, and using a table as a set.

lessons.title: The Table Library
lessons.summary: table.sort with and without a comparison function, sorting records and sorting by several keys, sorting a dictionary's keys for ordered output, table.concat, table.unpack and table.pack, and table.move.

lessons.title: Nested Tables and Copies
lessons.summary: Tables inside tables for grids and data, references and what really gets copied, shallow and deep copies, comparing tables by content, and printing a nested table so you can see it.

milestones.title: Functions
milestones.blurb: Functions and multiple results, optional and variable arguments, functions as values and closures, recursion, and scope.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.summary: Defining functions with function ... end, local functions, parameters and return, returning several values and where the extra values go, and functions that return nothing.

lessons.title: Optional and Variable Arguments
lessons.summary: Default values with or, when or is wrong for booleans, functions that take any number of arguments with ..., select and table.pack, and named arguments passed in a table.

lessons.title: Functions as Values and Closures
lessons.summary: Functions are values you can store, pass and return, anonymous functions, writing map, filter and reduce, closures that remember the variables around them, counters and factories, and the loop variable being fresh each round.

tasks.title: Functions that take and make functions

lessons.title: Recursion
lessons.summary: Functions that call themselves, the base case, why a local recursive function needs local function, walking nested tables, speeding up repeated work with memoisation, and Lua's proper tail calls.

lessons.title: Scope, Globals and Blocks
lessons.summary: Where a local is visible, blocks and do ... end, shadowing, how globals live in the table _G, why a typo creates a global, the const and close attributes of Lua 5.4, and keeping a file's names private.

milestones.title: Strings and Patterns
milestones.blurb: The string library, Lua patterns, gmatch and gsub, string.format and building text, and UTF-8.

lessons.title: The String Library
lessons.summary: Method syntax s:upper(), sub with positive and negative positions, upper, lower, rep, reverse, byte and char, find with plain text, and walking through a string character by character.

lessons.title: Patterns
lessons.summary: Lua patterns as a small alternative to regular expressions, the character classes %d %a %s %w and friends, sets in square brackets, the repeat signs + * - ?, anchors, captures, and string.match.

lessons.title: gmatch and gsub
lessons.summary: Looping over every match with gmatch, splitting text into words, lines and fields, replacing with gsub using a string, %1 captures, a table or a function, counting replacements, and %f for whole words.

tasks.title: Text tools with gmatch and gsub

lessons.title: string.format and Building Text
lessons.summary: The format directives %d %s %f %x %q, width, padding, alignment and precision, lining up a table of text, building long strings with a buffer table, and turning values into text with tostring and %q.

lessons.title: UTF-8 and Bytes
lessons.summary: Lua strings as bytes, why # counts bytes not letters, UTF-8 in brief, the utf8 library with len, char, codepoint and codes, taking characters safely, and the \u escape.

milestones.title: Metatables and Objects
milestones.blurb: Metatables and operators, __index and __newindex, classes with methods, inheritance, and modules.

lessons.title: Metatables and Operators
lessons.summary: What a metatable is, setmetatable and getmetatable, giving tables arithmetic with __add and friends, comparisons with __eq, __lt and __le, __tostring, __len, __concat and __call, and sharing one metatable between many tables.

lessons.title: __index and __newindex
lessons.summary: Default values for missing keys, __index as a table and as a function, rawget and rawset, watching and blocking writes with __newindex, read-only tables, catching typos in globals, and weak tables.

lessons.title: Classes and Objects
lessons.summary: Methods and the colon, self, the class pattern with a metatable whose __index is the class, a constructor called new, keeping methods shared and data per object, and the dot-versus-colon mistake.

lessons.title: Inheritance
lessons.summary: Making a subclass whose missing keys fall back to its base class, calling the base constructor and overridden methods, polymorphism with one loop over different kinds of object, checking what an object is, and when composition is simpler.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.summary: Splitting a program into files with require, the module pattern of a local table that the file returns, how require finds files with package.path and loads each one only once, module-private helpers, and dotted names for folders.

milestones.title: Lua in Depth
milestones.blurb: Errors and pcall, iterators and the generic for, coroutines, files and the os library, and how programs embed Lua.

lessons.title: Errors and pcall
lessons.summary: Raising errors with error and assert, the level argument that says whose fault it is, catching errors with pcall, error values that are tables, xpcall with a traceback, and the nil-plus-message convention for errors that are expected.

lessons.title: Iterators and the Generic for
lessons.summary: How for ... in really works with an iterator function, writing iterators as closures, stateless iterators like ipairs, next, iterating in sorted order, io.lines for reading input, and the __pairs gone from 5.4.

lessons.title: Coroutines
lessons.summary: Functions that pause with yield and continue with resume, passing values both ways, coroutine.status and wrap, generators, a producer and consumer, and the game-script pattern of many characters each running their own sequence.

lessons.title: Files and the os Library
lessons.summary: Opening files with io.open and its modes, reading with read and lines, writing and appending, closing reliably with close variables, saving and loading data as Lua tables, and time, dates, clocks and the environment from os.

lessons.title: Embedding Lua and Its Dialects
lessons.summary: How a C program runs Lua with the C API and its stack, giving scripts functions written in C, the garbage collector, Lua's versions and the dialects LuaJIT and Luau, and where to go next with LÖVE, Neovim and Roblox.

milestones.title: Deeper Lua
milestones.blurb: Environments and sandboxes for untrusted code, weak tables, finalizers and the garbage collector, and integers, bitwise operators and binary data.

lessons.title: Environments and Sandboxes
lessons.summary: Where global names really live - _G, the _ENV upvalue every chunk has, giving code its own environment, load with a custom environment, building a safe sandbox for untrusted scripts, limiting run time with debug.sethook, and modules without globals.

tasks.title: A script sandbox with a step limit

lessons.title: Weak Tables and the Garbage Collector
lessons.summary: How Lua frees memory and how to work with it - reachability, collectgarbage, weak keys and weak values with __mode, caches that do not leak, attaching data to objects without keeping them alive, __gc finalizers, and to-be-closed variables for resources that must be released on time.

tasks.title: A memoising cache that does not leak

lessons.title: Integers, Bitwise Operators and Binary Data
lessons.summary: Lua's 64-bit integers in depth - integer and float subtypes, floor division and wrap-around, the bitwise operators &, |, ~, <<, >> and ~x, flags and masks, unsigned comparison with math.ult, and reading and writing binary formats with string.pack and string.unpack.
